name: High resolution timer precision
plain: performance.now() returns a clock whose coarseness depends on browser and isolation.
meaning: Timer resolution is a deliberate defense against timing attacks. The resolution itself tells a site the browser and whether privacy mode or cross-origin isolation is on, and limits attacks like cache timing.

steps: Call performance.now() in a tight loop

limits.headline: Can use a clock whose sharpness shows your browser and privacy mode
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check how fine the page timer is
Guess your browser from that sharpness
Tell if privacy mode or cross origin protection is on
cannot: Get a very sharp clock without extra protections
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: performance.now() gives a very fast clock, but browsers deliberately make it coarser unless the site is isolated.

marketing.name: performance.now()
marketing.pitch: Returns a high resolution time for measuring how long things take, with precision limited for security.

marketing.name: Why COOP and COEP
marketing.pitch: Google explains that precise timers return only on pages that prove they are isolated from other sites.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why games and videos stay in sync. Browsers blur this clock on purpose to protect you from timing attacks, so most pages get a slightly rounded time.
story.for_makers: Games, audio tools and animation need good timing to run smoothly. Browsers round the timer to stop attacks and fingerprinting, and give a finer clock only to isolated pages. The rounding level is also a clue about your browser.

use_cases.example: A browser game uses the clock to step physics at an even rate, so movement does not jitter.
A web synth or DAW uses precise time to line up notes on the beat.
A video call tool measures delay to adjust how it buffers voice and picture.
A speed monitoring tool uses it to time page steps from real visitors.
Researchers have shown fine timers can be abused for timing attacks, so browsers round them.
A tracker tests how coarse the clock is to guess which browser and privacy mode you use.
A web animation tool uses precise timing to keep previews smooth.

technical_bounds: Cannot get nanosecond timing without cross-origin isolation (and still limited to about 5 microseconds)
Jitter added per page, repeated sampling can average it out

value.abuse: Side-channel attacks need finer timers; resolution fingerprints browser mode

history.change: Spectre: Chrome, Firefox, Safari coarsen performance.now() and Date; SharedArrayBuffer disabled
100 microsecond cap on all platforms; 5 microseconds if cross-origin isolated
Finer 20 microsecond precision only when cross-origin isolated
